findings.title: Delete skips the legacy delete on any storage error, dropping the NotFound tolerance
findings.body: The base code treated a NotFound from Storage.Delete as non-fatal and still deleted from LegacyStorage. This diff removes that guard. Now any error from `d.Storage.Delete` (line 101) returns early, so `d.Legacy.Delete` never runs. For an object that exists only in LegacyStorage, the k8s delete returns NotFound and the legacy row stays. The sibling DualWriterMode2.Delete (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode2.go:246-251) still tolerates NotFound on the legacy side and continues. Fix: keep the NotFound case non-fatal for the storage delete (log it and proceed to the legacy delete) and return the storage error only for other failures.
findings.originReason: The base guarded with !apierrors.IsNotFound(err) and then always called Legacy.Delete. This diff removed that guard.

verification.reason: In head, any error from Storage.Delete returns at line 104, before the legacy delete goroutine runs. The base treated NotFound as non-fatal and went on to Legacy.Delete, so an object that exists only in legacy is no longer deleted there.

findings.title: Legacy write failures in Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection are only counted, never logged
findings.body: The goroutines at lines 55-56, 112-113, 139-140 and 165-166 capture the legacy error only in the histogram. The base code logged these failures (for example `log.WithValues("object", created).Error(err, "unable to create object in legacy storage")` and the matching Update and DeleteCollection messages, all removed by this diff). Now a failed legacy write leaves LegacyStorage silently behind UnifiedStorage: no log line, no retry, no visible state, and the caller already received success. Fix: log the legacy error in each goroutine, as the base code did.
findings.originReason: The base logged these legacy errors. This diff replaced the logging with metrics only.

verification.reason: Each legacy goroutine only passes the error to recordLegacyDuration/recordStorageDuration and never logs it. The base logged legacy Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection failures.

findings.title: Storage failures are recorded in the legacy duration metric, and legacy results in the storage metric
findings.body: Create records a storage failure with recordLegacyDuration (line 45), and Update does the same at line 129. DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine records its result with recordStorageDuration (line 166). The histograms are split by store, so dashboards and alerts that compare the two stores will show the wrong numbers. Fix: use recordStorageDuration in the storage error branches at lines 45 and 129, and recordLegacyDuration at line 166.
findings.originReason: The metric calls are new in this diff. The base mode 3 recorded no metrics.

verification.reason: Lines 45 and 129 record a Storage.Create/Update failure in the legacy histogram. Line 166 records the result of Legacy.DeleteCollection in the storage histogram. metrics.go shows these are two separate HistogramVecs.

findings.title: Delete passes the object name as the metric's kind label, creating one series per object
findings.body: Line 106 calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. The third argument is the `kind` label (metrics.go:59-61 with labels is_error, mode, kind, method). Every deleted object name therefore creates a new Prometheus series in `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds`. Use `options.Kind`, as the other calls in the file do.
findings.originReason: This call was added by the diff.

verification.reason: Line 106 passes `name` as the third argument. That argument fills the kind label of dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds (metrics.go:59-61), so every deleted object name creates a new series.

findings.title: Legacy writes run on the request context and are likely cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: The detached goroutines in Create (line 51), Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163) derive their context from the request ctx passed into the method. The request context is cancelled when the HTTP handler returns (net/http documents this for Request.Context). The response is sent before those goroutines finish, so the legacy SQL write will probably fail with context canceled. That failure is only a metric (see the finding on silent failures). Mode 3's contract is 'write to both', and rolling back to a legacy-reading mode would lose the rows that were never written. Confirm this by creating a playlist in mode 3 and checking the SQL table. If confirmed, the legacy write needs a context detached from the request (for example context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) before the goroutine starts. Mode 1 uses the same request-derived pattern (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode1.go:53-54), so the same question applies there. Confidence is medium because the request-context lifetime comes from net/http and the apiserver, which I did not open.
findings.originReason: For mode 3, the base wrote to legacy synchronously on the live request context. The async goroutine is new in this diff (mode 1 has the same pattern on its own).

verification.reason: The goroutines derive their contexts from the request ctx with WithTimeoutCause, which does not detach from cancellation. Once the handler returns, the request context (net/http and the apiserver's per-request timeout) is cancelled, and the legacy store's DB call runs on that ctx. In the base these writes ran synchronously before the method returned.

findings.title: The 'mode 3' integration tests never reach mode 3
findings.body: DualWriterDesiredModes sets Mode3 in the ini (pkg/tests/testinfra/testinfra.go:389-395). builder/helper.go:169-173 passes that value to SetDualWritingMode. On a fresh KV store, pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter.go:188-196 sets the current mode to Mode1. The transition block at dualwriter.go:198-218 only moves 1->2 and 2->1, and nothing moves into Mode3. So SetDualWritingMode returns Mode1, and the new 'file, mode 3' (line 132), 'unified storage, mode 3' (line 191) and skipped etcd (line 287) cases all run Mode1. They duplicate the mode 1 cases and add no coverage. Fix: add a transition into Mode3 in SetDualWritingMode, or seed the KV store with Mode3 in the test. The conclusion depends on the KV store returning ok=false for a missing key (pkg/infra/kvstore/kvstore.go:47 delegates, which I did not read).
findings.originReason: The mode 3 integration test cases were added by this diff.

verification.reason: SetDualWritingMode defaults a missing KV entry to Mode1 and only handles the 1->2 and 2->1 transitions, so desiredMode Mode3 returns Mode1. The new 'mode 3' integration cases therefore run the mode 1 dual writer.

findings.title: Mode 3 tests never assert the legacy write, and some names misdescribe the test
findings.body: The Create success case is named 'creating an object only in the unified store' (line 28), but its setup (lines 30-32) expects a legacy Create, and Mode 3 writes to both stores. Because the mock `m` is shared between the two stores, the storage call consumes the legacy expectation, so the setup does not describe what runs. None of the Mode 3 tests assert that the legacy write happened, and the legacy write is asynchronous, so the core Mode 3 behaviour is untested. The List error case at line 145 is named 'is not implemented', but List is now implemented and the error comes from the mock. Rename the cases, and add a way to wait for the goroutine (or check the mock calls after it) to test the legacy write.
findings.originReason: The test file was rewritten from commented-out code in this diff.

verification.reason: The Create success case is named 'only in the unified store' but sets up a legacy Create on the shared mock. No test asserts on mock calls or waits for the goroutines. Line 145 still says 'is not implemented' even though List is implemented.

findings.title: Update sends the raw objInfo to legacy, so legacy recomputes the update against its own object
findings.body: The base code computed `updated` once from the storage object and passed legacy an updateWrapper carrying the storage result, so both stores received the same object. Now line 139 passes the raw objInfo, and legacy calls UpdatedObject against its own old object. For a full PUT the results match. For PATCH or apply, the legacy copy can differ from the unified copy, and nothing compares them. Was this intended? If the goal is identical writes, pass the storage result as the base code did.
findings.originReason: The base wrapped the storage result in updateWrapper for the legacy update. This diff removed that.

verification.reason: Head passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update. The playlist legacy Update calls objInfo.UpdatedObject against its own Get result, so it no longer receives the storage result the base passed via updateWrapper.

findings.title: Delete builds a logger with name/kind/method values, then puts d.Log into the context
findings.body: Line 96 builds `log` with the name, kind and method values, but line 97 stores `d.Log` in the context. Nested calls then lose those values. The sibling methods use `log` here (Create at line 39, Update at line 123). Pass `log`.
findings.originReason: The base put `log` into the context. This diff changed it to d.Log.

verification.reason: Line 96 builds `log` with name/kind/method values, but line 97 stores d.Log in the context, unlike Create/Update/Get/List.

findings.title: Update doc comment describes a sequential write that is now asynchronous
findings.body: The comment says Update 'writes first to Storage and then to LegacyStorage'. The legacy write now runs in a goroutine after the response is returned (lines 134-141). Update the comment to say that the legacy write is asynchronous and best effort.

verification.reason: The comment's order (storage first, then legacy) is still literally correct. But it does not say that the legacy write is now a fire-and-forget goroutine whose result never reaches the caller, so this is a minor doc gap.

contracts.action: Create (storage first, then legacy in a detached goroutine, returns storage result)
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode2.go:39-72 (legacy first, then storage, synchronous); pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode1.go:37-75 (legacy then detached storage goroutine with DeepCopy)
contracts.before_after: Base: storage Create, then legacy Create synchronously, legacy error logged, returns storage result. Now: the legacy Create runs in a goroutine with a 10s timeout and its error is only recorded in a histogram; the method returns before it finishes.
contracts.visible_effect: The caller gets the unified-storage object. The legacy write is invisible to the caller.
contracts.failure_mode: Legacy failure is silent (only a metric, dualwriter_mode3.go:55-56). The goroutine's context is derived from the request context (line 51), so the legacy write is probably cancelled when the handler returns. Nothing retries it.
contracts.open_question: Does the request context survive after the k8s apiserver handler returns? If not, the legacy write is cancelled. Check whether the apiserver handler wraps the request context in context.WithoutCancel, or whether the handler outlives the response.

contracts.action: Get (reads from storage only, passes the caller's GetOptions through)
contracts.before_after: Base: Storage.Get with an empty &metav1.GetOptions{}. Now: the caller's options, so ResourceVersion is forwarded to storage.
contracts.visible_effect: The result is the storage object. A client-supplied resourceVersion now affects the read.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is logged and returned. There is no legacy fallback, which is correct for mode 3. Nothing is silent.

contracts.action: List (now reads storage instead of the nil,nil stub)
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode2.go:114-188 (merges legacy and storage); Storage.List is called directly here
contracts.before_after: Base: a TODO stub that logged 'List not implemented' and returned nil, nil. Now: returns Storage.List results.
contracts.visible_effect: Lists now show unified-storage content. Mode 3 no longer returns a nil object.
contracts.failure_mode: Error is logged and returned. No silent path.

contracts.before_after: Base: storage delete with NotFound tolerated, then legacy delete. Now: any storage error returns immediately, so the legacy delete is skipped even for NotFound. On success the legacy delete runs in a goroutine, and the metric label uses name in the kind slot (line 106).
contracts.visible_effect: The caller gets the storage result or error. A NotFound now leaves the legacy row behind.
contracts.failure_mode: The legacy row stays and is never reconciled (dualwriter_mode3.go:101-104, 112-113). Legacy delete errors are silent.

contracts.action: Update (storage update with raw objInfo, legacy goroutine with the same raw objInfo)
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode2.go:274-333 (computes updated object once, passes updateWrapper with the result to legacy)
contracts.before_after: Base: fetched the old object from storage, computed UpdatedObject, wrote storage, then wrote legacy with the storage result. Now: no pre-fetch. Storage gets raw objInfo and legacy gets raw objInfo in a goroutine.
contracts.visible_effect: The caller gets the storage result. The legacy record may differ for PATCH or apply.
contracts.failure_mode: Storage error is recorded under the legacy metric (line 129). Legacy error is silent (line 139-140).

contracts.before_after: Base: storage DeleteCollection error was logged and legacy still ran. Now: a storage error returns immediately and the legacy DeleteCollection is skipped. On success the legacy call runs in a goroutine and records to the storage metric (line 166).
contracts.visible_effect: The caller gets the storage result or error.
contracts.failure_mode: A storage failure now leaves legacy untouched. Legacy failures are silent and mislabelled in metrics.

contracts.action: Mode 3 selected through the playlist unified_storage_mode config (SetDualWritingMode)
contracts.before_after: Desired Mode3 with no stored value sets Mode1 and returns Mode1, so the test runs mode 1.
contracts.visible_effect: The mode 3 integration cases do not exercise Mode3.
contracts.failure_mode: The tests pass without covering Mode3, so a Mode3 regression would go unnoticed.
contracts.open_question: Does the KV store return ok=false for a missing key on a fresh instance? If it does, the conclusion holds.

summary: Reviewed the Mode 3 dual writer, its unit tests, the mode 1 test edit, the playlist integration tests and go.work.sum. The main problems: (1) Delete no longer tolerates NotFound from storage, so the legacy row is skipped; (2) legacy write failures are only counted in metrics, not logged, which is a regression; (3) storage and legacy metrics are mislabelled in several places, and Delete puts the object name into the kind label; (4) legacy writes run on the request context, which is probably cancelled when the handler returns, so they likely fail. Medium confidence, needs a check against a real SQL row. (5) The new 'mode 3' playlist integration cases never reach Mode 3, because SetDualWritingMode has no transition into it. Test naming and coverage issues and a duplicate go.work.sum line are lower severity. I could not run tests or confirm the request-context lifetime from code outside this part.
